newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks firmer in light London trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks firmer in light London trade.

text.p: Japanese shares edged higher on Wednesday in light London trade on follow-through buying from Tokyo after the U.S. election result, traders said. London's Nikkei/ISE index closed up 2.88 points at 1,436.29 after U.S. election news had sent the Nikkei-225 index 399.19 points higher to 20,991.52 overnight.

President Bill Clinton comfortably held on to the White House while the Republicans retained control of the Senate and House of Representatives, lifting hopes of economic stability and restrained government spending.
But traders said that today's gains could be short-lived because of the continuing political uncertainty in Japan.
"It looks good for the opening in Tokyo tomorrow, but the highs in the market could be short-lived and the Nikkei could drift back down to 21,000," said one trader.
Shares in companies benefitting most from the dollar/yen exchange rate provided interest, among them Sharp and Fujitsu.
Sharp shares closed at 1,755 yen in London, up on their overnight close of 1,750 yen. Fujitsu shares edged up to 1,022-1/2 yen, after closing at 1,020 yen in Tokyo.
